title: Play-Nice Shared Status Vocabulary
description: Closed semantic vocabulary for system state. Projects map provider-specific states into this vocabulary so every surface (CLI, API, UI, agents) speaks the same truth. Distinctions that matter: unavailable != not_configured; unknown != healthy; stale != current; implemented != verified; running != correct; failed != unavailable. Words are of two kinds: health (healthy, warning, needs_attention, degraded, unavailable, not_configured, disabled, stale, unknown) describes how a thing is now; progress (working, waiting, blocked, deferred, partial, complete, failed) describes how an operation is going.
$comment: Machine vocabulary. A human UI may render any of these as plain language (e.g. healthy -> 'Everything looks good.') but must never collapse distinct states into one another.

meanings.healthy: observed ok right now, with recent evidence
meanings.unavailable: cannot be reached or is not responding - not necessarily failed, and not the same as not configured
meanings.not_configured: nothing wired up - a vacancy, not a failure
meanings.stale: last observation too old to trust; do not re-show as current
meanings.unknown: no evidence either way - NOT healthy, NOT failed
meanings.working: an operation is actively in progress
meanings.waiting: paused on an external event or timer
meanings.blocked: cannot proceed without a decision or dependency
meanings.deferred: intentionally postponed, with a record of why
meanings.partial: some of a multi-part thing is true (e.g. migration parity)
meanings.failed: a finished operation that did not succeed; the reason goes in a separate field, not in a new word
